market_summary: Markets are digesting a shock leadership crisis at Nvidia (CEO Jensen Huang resigned abruptly on Nov 12 amid a scandal, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO), triggering a wave of same-day analyst downgrades and a stock slide, even as broader US futures/indices (SPY, QQQ) stabilized and bounced the next session. In Singapore, bank earnings were mixed (OCBC beat, DBS and UOB missed) while Singtel posted a strong H1 beat with raised guidance and Singapore Airlines' profit nearly halved despite record revenue, even as its share price kept rallying. Rate-sensitive and growth tech (GOOGL, AAPL) are seeing a modest bounce after recent drawdowns, while mega-cap growth sentiment overall remains shaky given Meta and Microsoft's recent pullbacks.

picks.thesis: CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation amid scandal has triggered a near-unprecedented single-day wave of sell-side downgrades (at least 9 firms cutting ratings/targets on Nov 12), signaling a serious loss of confidence in leadership continuity right as the stock already sits -30% from its 52w high and -27% over 1 month. With Q3 earnings due Nov 17, volatility and further de-rating risk are elevated while an interim CFO-CEO transition creates strategic uncertainty into a critical AI capex cycle.
picks.news: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on 2026-11-12 following an affairs scandal; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO; shares fell 4.3% and at least 9 banks downgraded ratings/cut targets same day (SEC 8-K filing and PBS NewsHour, 2026-11-12).
picks.risks: Nvidia fundamentals and AI demand remain intact; if Kress stabilizes the narrative quickly or Nov 17 earnings beat strongly, the stock could snap back sharply given how oversold it already is (analyst consensus target still implies +86% upside, reflecting prior bullishness that may reassert).

picks.thesis: Singtel's underlying H1 FY2027 net profit rose 10% to S$1.49bn and management raised full-year guidance, yet the stock barely moved (+0.2%), suggesting the market hasn't fully priced the improved outlook. Analyst sentiment is overwhelmingly positive (13 buy / 2 hold / 0 sell) with consensus target implying ~26% upside, and the stock trades well below its 52-week high.
picks.news: Singtel reported H1 FY2027 underlying net profit up 10% to S$1.49bn and raised FY2027 guidance, reported 2026-11-12 (Business Times); note headline net profit fell due to lack of one-off divestment gains versus prior year.
picks.risks: Headline net profit fell 55% y/y due to the absence of prior-year divestment gains, which could cause near-term confusion or a negative reaction if investors focus on the headline figure rather than underlying growth; regional telco competition and associate (Bharti, Telkomsel) weakness could also cap upside.

picks.thesis: Singapore Airlines' H1 FY2026/27 profit fell 43.9% to S$134m despite record revenue, pointing to margin compression from costs/competition, yet the stock has rallied +11.2% over the past month and sits near its 52-week high. Analyst consensus is tepid (1 buy, 10 hold, 3 sell) with an implied downside of -3.3% to target, suggesting the rally has outpaced fundamentals.
picks.news: SIA reported H1 FY2026/27 profit down 43.9% y/y to S$134m on record revenue, reported 2026-11-11 (AsiaOne).
picks.risks: Elevated travel demand, fuel cost relief, or a favorable dividend/buyback announcement could extend the rally; low analyst coverage conviction on the short side (only 3 sells) means consensus doesn't strongly support a sharp drop.

picks.thesis: Alphabet has pulled back sharply (-25.8% from 52w high, -15.6% over 1 month) despite near-unanimous bullish analyst coverage (53 buy, 5 hold, 0 sell) and a consensus target implying +34% upside. The stock jumped +3.9% in the latest session, potentially marking the start of a reversal from oversold technical levels (price well below both 50- and 200-day moving averages).
picks.news: No fresh company-specific catalyst in the provided news; move reflects a broader growth-stock de-rating also seen in Meta, offset by one recent analyst note (Citizens Market Outperform→Market Perform on 2026-10-29, now 10+ trading days old).
picks.risks: If the sell-off in high-multiple AI/growth names (mirroring Nvidia's leadership-driven slide) continues, GOOGL could retest lows; regulatory/antitrust overhangs for Alphabet remain a persistent risk not captured in this news set.

picks.thesis: UOB missed Q3 2026 earnings expectations (vs. OCBC which beat), and it is the weakest of the three Singapore banks technically — down 16% from its 52-week high, trading below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages, with the most negative 1-month and 3-month returns of the group. Analyst sentiment is also the most lukewarm (5 buy, 9 hold, 2 sell).
picks.news: UOB missed Q3 2026 earnings expectations while OCBC beat, reported 2026-11-06/11 (thefinance.sg sector roundup).
picks.risks: This is sector-wide weakness shared with DBS/OCBC tied to broader rate and margin pressure, not UOB-specific; a rebound in regional banking sentiment or a dividend surprise could lift the stock alongside peers.

picks.thesis: Keppel has been heavily sold off (-24.9% from 52w high, -11.5% over 3 months, trading well below both moving averages) yet retains a strongly bullish analyst base (12 buy, 2 hold, 1 sell) with consensus target implying ~28.5% upside, the highest in the SGX watchlist. This looks like a value/contrarian setup if the broader market stabilizes.
picks.news: No fresh company-specific catalyst in the provided news; this view rests mainly on technical oversold conditions and analyst target gap.
picks.risks: News is thin here — without a fresh catalyst, the stock could remain range-bound or drift lower further if broader SGX/REIT-adjacent sentiment stays weak; this is a lower-conviction, valuation-based call rather than an event-driven one.
